THREE NEW DEANS 


FROM THE INFORMATION OFFICE 
Vi. h-013! Local i340 
GERALD WRIGHT DIRECTOR 


AT SGWU 


METROPOLITAN YMCA 
OF MONTREAL 


SIR GEORGE WILLIAMS 
UNIVERSITY AND SCHOOLS 


JUNE 28, 1963 


THREE NEW MAJOR APPOINTMENTS IN THE ACADEMIC ADMINISTRATION OF SIR 
GEORGE WILLIAMS UNIVERSITY HAVE BEEN ANNOUNCED BY VICE-PRINCIAL 

DOUGLASS BURNS CLARKE. DR. SAMUEL MADRAS HAS BEEN APPOINTED DEAN OF THE 
FACULTY OF SCIENCE. DR. JOHN W. O'BRIEN HAS BEEN APPOINTED DEAN OF THE 
FACULTY OF ARTS. PROF. JACK BORDAN HAS BEEN APPOINTED DEAN OF THE 


FACULTY OF ENGINEERING. 


THESE APPOINTMENTS MARK AN HISTORICAL CHANGE IN THE ACADEMIC STRUCTURE 
OF THE UNIVERSITY. UNTIL THIS YEAR, ALL FACULTIES WERE ADMINISTERED 
3Y THE VICE=-PRINCIPAL. THE APPOINTMENT OF THREE FACULTY DEANS WILL 
CREATE MUCH SMALLER EDUCATION UNITS, THEREBY RETAINING THE OPPORTUNITY 


FOR CONTINUED EASY CONTACT BETWEEN FACULTY AND STUDENTS. 


IN MAKING THE APPOINTMENTS KNOWN, PROF. CLARKE STATED THAT, “ONE OF 

THE GREAT PROBLEMS FACING SIR GEORGE AND OTHER UNIVERSITIES IS TO PRO- 
VIDE EDUCATION FOR THOUSANDS MORE PEOPLE AND YET RETAIN A CLOSE TOUCH 
BETWEEN THE STUDENT AND HIS FACULTY PERSONNEL. IN 1956, OUR FIRST YEAR 
AT THE PRESENT NEW BUILDING, WE HAD 798 DAY STUDENTS AND 300 EVENING 
STUDENTS, COMPARED WITH PRESENT ENROLLMENT OF 2,500 AND 6,),00. THE 


PROJECTED EXPANSION FOR 1967 IS 5,000 AND 10,000." 


VICE-PRINCIPAL CLARKE ALSO ANNOUNCED THAT DR. H.F. QUINN, WHO HAS BEEN 
FOR MANY YEARS CHAIRMAN OF. THE DEPARTMENT OF POLITICAL SCIENCE, HAS 
\CCEPTED THE POST OF SENIOR PROFESSOR IN THE SOCIAL SCIENCES DIVISION. 


DR. QUINN WAS ONE OF THE EARLY GRADUATES OF THE UNIVERSITY AND HAS LONG 
BEEN A FAMILIAR FIGURE TO THE STUDENTS OF SIR GEORGE WILLIAMS.
